From 4b5d099e1049909a16e93648d80df18a516afb73 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jonathan McPherson <jonathan@rstudio.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Dec 2017 14:58:50 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] save console process before computing interaction mode; fixes
 #1810

this change fixes an issue; because getInteractionMode()
uses the saved console process, it needs to be set before we check the
interaction mode.

diff --git a/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java b/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
index dbedddd688..0e5b0af8e6 100644
--- a/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
+++ b/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
@@ -76,6 +76,9 @@ public class ConsoleProgressDialog extends ProgressDialog
          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Invalid combination of arguments to ConsoleProgressDialog");
       }
+
+      // save console process so that we can compute interaction mode below
+      consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;
       
       if (getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER)
       {
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary

**File modified:** `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java`

**Modification:** In the constructor of `ConsoleProgressDialog`, the assignment `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` was moved earlier, so that it happens **before** the call to `getInteractionMode()` rather than after it.

**Relationship / Reasoning:**
The method `getInteractionMode()` relies on the instance field `consoleProcess_` to determine the interaction mode. Previously, the field was set only after `getInteractionMode()` was invoked, meaning the method was operating on a stale or null value of `consoleProcess_`. By reordering the code to assign `consoleProcess_` first, the fix ensures that `getInteractionMode()` uses the correct, up-to-date console process reference when determining whether the interaction mode is `INTERACTION_NEVER`. This resolves the bug (#1810) where incorrect interaction mode computation could cause faulty dialog behavior.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`if (getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER)`
`attachToProcess(consoleProcess);`
Reason: `getInteractionMode()` is called before `consoleProcess_` field is assigned. Since `attachToProcess(consoleProcess)` (which presumably sets `consoleProcess_`) is invoked only at the end of the constructor, `consoleProcess_` is still null (or stale) when `getInteractionMode()` executes, causing it to compute the interaction mode based on incorrect state rather than the actual passed-in `consoleProcess` parameter.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;`
Reason: By explicitly assigning the `consoleProcess` parameter to the `consoleProcess_` field immediately after the null-check and before calling `getInteractionMode()`, the field is properly initialized in time for the interaction mode computation to use the correct, up-to-date console process reference, ensuring `getInteractionMode()` returns the correct value.
